summary: Added the persistence layer for the lifecycle-uc10-uc11 module's 10 tables (ORM entities + one Alembic migration each, chained after the existing CreateObligationAuditLog head) and registered them in app/models/__init__.py. The shared foundation infrastructure (header-auth/role enforcement in app/auth.py, centralized error handling in app/main.py, paging primitives in app/schemas/pagination.py, CORS, DB wiring in app/db.py) was already built by an earlier foundation task and fully satisfies this contract's requirements, so it was reused as-is rather than rebuilt. No business endpoints were implemented, per the task's scope -- the existing /health route proves the wiring. Updated the pre-existing tests/test_persistence.py (which hard-coded assertions tied to a prior module's context.json, e.g. a 'CreateContractsLifecycleColumns' migration name and contracts-table column renames that do not exist in this run) so it validates against the current context.json instead. Verified with python -m compileall, pytest (303 passed), alembic's offline --sql upgrade render, and a live boot of the app on port 5199 with a passing /health check.

pr.title: Foundation: persistence layer for lifecycle-uc10-uc11 (tracker + settings tables)
pr.body: Adds the 10 ORM entities and 10 Alembic migrations (CreateContractLifecycleStageHistory ... CreateTenantAuditLog, chained after the existing CreateObligationAuditLog head) that back the lifecycle-uc10-uc11 module's tracker and tenant-settings endpoints. No business endpoints are implemented here -- that is left to the resource tasks that follow. Shared infrastructure (header-auth/role enforcement, centralized error handling, paging primitives, CORS, DB wiring) already existed from an earlier foundation task and needed no changes. Also repairs tests/test_persistence.py, which still asserted a previous module's migration-chain name and contracts-table deviations; it now validates against the current context.json.

blockers: TASK.md's verification steps name dotnet/Api.sln commands, but this repo's actual stack (per the repo-root CLAUDE.md, which governs HOW per the run instructions) is Python/FastAPI with pytest/alembic -- verified instead with `python -m compileall app alembic`, `pytest -q` (303 passed), `alembic upgrade head --sql` (offline DDL render, no live Postgres in this sandbox), and a live `uvicorn` boot answering GET /health 200.

The shared foundation infrastructure this task was asked to build (centralized error handling, header-auth/role enforcement, paging primitives, CORS) already exists in app/main.py, app/auth.py, app/schemas/pagination.py and app/db.py from an earlier foundation task in this repo's history, and already matches this contract's roles (TENANT_ADMIN, CONTRACT_OWNER, LEGAL_REVIEWER, APPROVER) and error-body shape. It was left untouched and reused rather than rebuilt, per CLAUDE.md's module-addition rule against rewriting code a new module doesn't need to touch.

tests/test_persistence.py pre-existed in the repo but was written against a different (earlier) module's context.json: it hard-coded an expected migration-chain element 'CreateContractsLifecycleColumns' and column-rename/nullability-deviation/shared-table exceptions for a 'contracts' table that this module's context.json does not reference at all. Since context.json is reloaded fresh per run, those assertions failed against the current (lifecycle-uc10-uc11) contract. Rewrote the test to assert against the current context.json's tables/migrations with no hard-coded exceptions, since none of this module's 10 tables pre-date it or are shared with another module.
No fields were added beyond context.json's table/DTO definitions, and no endpoint outside this task's scope (persistence + shared infra only) was implemented.
